corpusSummary: A broad, multidisciplinary corpus examining how large language models are used, evaluated, and governed across domains. The records reveal empirical work on user trust and adoption, AI-assisted decision making, education, health communication, and policy research. They stress contextualized evaluation, safety and fairness, and the growing role of AI as a methodological tool and pedagogical aid.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction, trust, and social dynamics
themes.description: Studies explore user trust, adoption decisions, social influence, wellbeing, and embodiment in human–AI collaborations across education, health, and daily life.

themes.name: LLM behavior, bias, safety, and robustness
themes.description: Researchers investigate bias, misinformation susceptibility, credibility, polarization, and safety of LLM outputs across applications and populations.

themes.name: AI as research tool and methodological innovations
themes.description: Work proposes and evaluates LLM-enabled methods for content analysis, policy study, heritage reconstruction, and multi-agent simulations in social science.

themes.name: Health and wellbeing implications of AI
themes.description: Papers address AI-driven health communication, patient education, digital health equity, and misinformation within health contexts.

themes.name: AI in education and learning
themes.description: Research examines AI’s impact on pedagogy, assessment, literacy, teacher–learner dynamics, and strategies for responsible integration in learning environments.
